title: SSS-Class Revival Hunter Anime's New Video Reveals Ending Song
content:
The staff for the television anime of writer Sinnoa 's SSS-Class Revival Hunter web novel and adaptor Neida and artist Bill K 's webtoon revealed the anime's ending theme song "Fading" by THE SPELLBOUND × BOOM BOOM SATELLITES groups in a new promotional video, on Wednesday.

Crunchyroll describes the story:

A mysterious tower crawling with monsters has suddenly appeared, drawing Hunters willing to risk their lives for glory and riches. Gongja Kim, a weak F-rank Hunter, spends his days envying the Flame Emperor who reigns as the top Hunter. But his chance at greatness finally arrives when he joins forces with the Sword Emperor and gains a rare S-rank skill, with one catch: he must die to activate it.

The anime stars:

• Takeo Ōtsuka as Gongja Kim (listed as Yeon-ja Kim on the anime's website)

• Satoshi Hino as the Sword Emperor

• Toshiki Masuda as Flame Emperor

• Megumi Han as Witch of the Black Dragon

• Sayaka Kinoshita as Paladin

• Risa Shimizu as Countess

• Makoto Furukawa as Poisonous Viper

• Natsumi Fujiwara as Inquisitor

• Yuka Iguchi as Master Alchemist

• Shunsuke Sakuya as Blade Saint

Hiroaki Sakurai ( The Demon Girl Next Door ) is directing the anime at Studio fu . Sayuri Ōba ( Romantic Killer ) is writing the script. Takahiro Yoshimatsu ( Trigun ) is designing the characters. HAYATE is producing the series. Ryo Kawasaki ( To Your Eternity three seasons, Romantic Killer ) and Tomoyuki Kono ( A Few Moments of Cheers , Romantic Killer ) are composing the music.

The anime will debut in January on Fuji TV 's +Ultra programming block. Crunchyroll will stream the anime worldwide, excluding Asia, with availability in the Indian subcontinent, Indonesia, Singapore, the Philippines, and Malaysia.

The original novel debuted in November 2018, and the webtoon launched in December 2020. Tapas publishes the webtoon in English digitally, and Ize Press is releasing the series in print. WuxiaWorld publishes the web novel in English.
author: ANN

title: Tomoko Ninomiya's Nanatsu-ya: Shinobu and Her Jewelry Box Manga Gets TV Anime in 2027
content:
A website opened on Wednesday to announce the television anime adaptation of Tomoko Ninomiya 's Nanatsu-ya: Shinobu and Her Jewelry Box ( Nanatsuya Shinobu no Hōsekibako ) manga. The website also revealed the anime's teaser trailer, teaser visual, main staff members, and 2027 debut.

Ninomiya also drew an illustration to celebrate the announcement:

Kodansha 's K MANGA service publishes the manga in English and describes the story:

Shinobu, a second-year in high school, is part of the family that runs Kurata-ya, a storied pawn shop based in a breezy central Tokyo neighborhood. She helps run the place when school isn't calling, and she has a natural gift that aids her a great deal—the ability to see the “aura” released by gemstones! Shinobu doesn't have a boyfriend, but she does have a fiancé handpicked for her by her grandfather—Akisada Kitagami, a man from a prestigious family who wound up being taken in by Kurata-ya at a young age. He now works as a salesman for a first-class jewelry brand, but he's also got more than his fair share of secrets...

Chiaki Kon ( Nodame Cantabile: Finale , Nodame Cantabile: Paris , The Way of the Househusband ) is directing the anime at J.C.STAFF . Seishi Minakami ( A Certain Scientific Railgun , Sugar Apple Fairy Tale , Sacrificial Princess & the King of Beasts ) is in charge of series scripts, and Mai Furuki ( I.Cinnamoroll , Mewkledreamy ) is designing the characters.

Ninomiya launched the ongoing manga in Kodansha 's Kiss magazine in November 2013, and Kodansha will publish the manga's 28th compiled book volume on November 13.

The manga had gone on several hiatuses from 2018-2019 due to the author's health.

Ninomiya launched her Nodame Cantabile manga in Kiss magazine in 2001, and ended it in 2009. Del Rey published 16 volumes of the manga in North America until the publisher ceased releasing manga. Kodansha USA Publishing later published all 25 volumes in English digitally. The manga was adapted into three television anime series , and has also received live-action drama and film adaptations .
author: ANN

title: Nanatsu-ya: Shinobu and Her Jewelry Box Anime Announced for 2027, Reveals Teaser Visual and Trailer
content:
The anime adaptation of Tomoko Ninomiya’s Nanatsu-ya: Shinobu and Her Jewelry Box has been officially announced for 2027. A teaser visual, teaser trailer, and the main staff were revealed alongside the announcement.

The main staff includes:

• Director: Chiaki Kon

• Series Composition: Seishi Minakami

• Character Design: Mai Furuki

• Animation Production: J.C.STAFF

Kon previously directed Nodame Cantabile: Paris Arc and Nodame Cantabile Finale , while J.C.STAFF also produced the Nodame Cantabile anime adaptations.

Director Chiaki Kon commented:

I’m grateful to have the opportunity to be involved in Tomoko Ninomiya-sensei’s work once again. The stories that unfold from gemstones are truly fascinating. I’m going to enjoy bringing these gemstone stories to life beautifully in anime for you all, so I hope you will do your best at watching.

Nanatsu-ya: Shinobu and Her Jewelry Box is a Japanese manga written and illustrated by Tomoko Ninomiya. It began serialization in Kodansha’s Kiss magazine in November 2013, releasing 27 volumes so far. Volume 28 is scheduled to release in Japan on November 13. It’s also available on K MANGA , where the story is described: The new series from Tomoko Ninomiya, creator of Nodame Cantabile, turns its focus on the world of jewelry! Shinobu, a second-year in high school, is part of the family that runs Kurata-ya, a storied pawn shop based in a breezy central Tokyo neighborhood. She helps run the place when school isn’t calling, and she has a natural gift that aids her a great deal—the ability to see the “aura” released by gemstones! Shinobu doesn’t have a boyfriend, but she does have a fiancé handpicked for her by her grandfather—Akisada Kitagami, a man from a prestigious family who wound up being taken in by Kurata-ya at a young age. He now works as a salesman for a first-class jewelry brand, but he’s also got more than his fair share of secrets… “

content:

The anime will premiere in 2027.

Staff Director: Chiaki Kon ( Golden Time, Niehime to Kemono no Ou ) Series Composition: Shinsuke Oonishi ( Basilisk: Ouka Ninpouchou ) Character Design: Mai Furuki ( Mewkledreamy ) Studio: J.C.Staff

The series is published in English through the K Manga platform.

Shinobu doesn't have a boyfriend, but she does have a fiancé handpicked for her by her grandfather—Akisada Kitagami, a man from a prestigious family who wound up being taken in by Kurata-ya at a young age. He now works as a salesman for a first-class jewelry brand, but he's also got more than his fair share of secrets… (Source: Kodansha)

title: Berserk of Gluttony Season 2 Premieres Next April
content:
The staff for the second television anime season based on Ichika Isshiki and fame's Berserk of Gluttony ( Bōshoku no Berserk: Ore Dake Level to Iu Gainen wo Toppa Suru ) light novel series announced the opening of the new season's website, and also revealed its teaser visual and April 2027 premiere. The visual's caption teases: "New stage Domain of E begins."

First season director Tetsuya Yanagisawa is the second season's overall director, and Ken'ichi Ishikura ( D.C.III ~Da Capo III~ , Sakura Trick ) is directing the new season at ACGT. Mariko Kunisawa returns to write the series scripts, and Takafumi Furusawa is again designing the characters.

Returning cast members include:

• Ryōta Ōsaka as Fate Graphite

• Tomokazu Seki as Greed

• Hisako Tōjō as Roxy Heart

• Misato Matsuoka as Myne

• Hitomi Sekine as Eris

• Takehito Koyasu as Aaron

Seven Seas Entertainment is releasing both the novel series and its manga adaptation in English, and it describes the story:

Fate Graphite is one of the forsaken. Cursed with the skill “Gluttony,” he is ever starving, never sateduntil the day he kills a dying thief and devours the man's strength—and his soul. The true hunger of Fate's Gluttony has awakened, and if he can learn to control his power, he will at last be the master of his own destiny.

The anime's first season debuted in October 2023. Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired, and also streams an English dub .

After releasing the story on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō service, Isshiki launched the first novel volume with illustrations by fame in November 2017. Micro Magazine is also releasing the novels in a larger bunko format. Daisuke Takino launched the manga adaptation on Micro Magazine 's Comic Ride website in April 2018.
author: ANN

title: Berserk of Gluttony Season 2 Reveals Teaser Visual, April 2027 Release Date
content:
Berserk of Gluttony Season 2 will officially premiere in April 2027, with a new teaser visual revealed for the announcement. An official website for the second season has also opened. The anime previously confirmed that it would return next year .

The returning cast includes:

• Ryota Osaka as Fate

• Tomokazu Seki as Greed

• Hisako Tojo as Roxy

• Misato Matsuoka as Myne

• Hitomi Sekine as Eris

• Takehito Koyasu as Aaron

Tetsuya Yanagisawa serves as chief director, with Kenichi Ishikura directing the second season. Mariko Kunisawa is in charge of the series composition, with Takafumi Furusawa as the character designer, and studio A.C.G.T back to handle the animation production.

Season 2 will follow Fate after his return to the royal capital, where he will begin a new chapter as a Holy Knight while getting involved in another conflict surrounding the truth of the world. His Gluttony skill allows him to steal the skills and abilities of those he defeats, while his sentient black sword Greed continues to fight alongside him.

The new teaser visual shows Fate without the skull mask he previously used to conceal his identity from Roxy. Myne also appears overlooking him beneath a red moon, while the new season will move into a storyline involving the E Domain, which Fate surpassed during the first season. You can check out the new visual below.

Ichika Isshiki is the original author of the Berserk of Gluttony ( Boushoku no Berserk: Ore Dake Level to Iu Gainen o Toppa Sur ) series, which first started as a web novel on the Shosetsuka ni Naro website. It is currently serialized by Micro Magazine as a novel in GC Novels and GCN Bunko with illustrations by fame. There is also a manga adaptation, which has art by Daisuke Takino. The total circulation has surpassed 2.2 million copies. The official synopsis: In a world where the superiority of skills is absolute, a boy named Fate is scorned and belittled for his incompetence. This is because his skill, “Gluttony,” is completely useless except for making him hungry. Fate is forced to live at the bottom of society, enduring violence and being burdened with menial tasks by the prestigious Brellick family, who are among the highest-ranking Holy Knights in this world. The only solace he finds is in Roxy Heart, who, despite also being a Holy Knight, treats him with respect and kindness. However, everything changes when Fate accidentally kills a thief who infiltrates the castle while accompanying Roxy. In that moment, his Gluttony skill activates, allowing him to steal the opponent’s power and abilities. Fate’s skill is an incredible ability to take away skills and abilities from those he kills. Empowered by his newfound fighting abilities, Fate encounters Greed, a sentient sword with a skill known as “Greed,” also associated with one of the Deadly Sins. Together, they step into a world of conflict and struggle. Driven by the desire to protect his loved ones and defy the unjust world, Fate devours his enemies in order to consume their power. The destiny of this once-lowly boy, crawling on the ground, rapidly begins to unfold.
author: Anime Corner

title: ≠ME Idol Momo Sakurai Voice-Acts, Sings in Gacha Girls Corps Anime
content:
The staff for the television anime of author Chinkururi and illustrator Yasutaka Isegawa 's Gacha Girls Corps ( Gacha o Mawashite Nakama o Fuyasu: Saikyō no Bishōjo Gundan o Tsukuriagero ) light novel series presented a promotional video on Wednesday featuring the rabbit character Mofutto, in celebration of 11/11 or "Tachi Mimi Usagi no Hi" (Rabbit with Upright Ears Day). The video announces Momo Sakurai of the idol group ≠ME as the character's voice. The video also reveals and previews the instrumental version of the anime's ending theme song "Mofu-kyun Heart♡" (Mofutto ver) by Mofutto, as voiced by Sakurai.

Momo Sakurai as Mofutto

Kaiten Books describes the story:

UR-GUARANTEED—TO HAVE THE ADVENTURE OF A LIFETIME! Ready for an adventure that's out of this world? We've gacha covered. Norl's a cutting-edge cutie with a cutting edge who's a cut above the rest. Heihachi's just your average mobile game addict with a whale-sized hole in his wallet. But one day, he pulls an item that pulls him into another world, spinning his life around with a spin of the gacha. Attacked by monsters, and left without options, Heihachi does what he knows best—roll gacha! To his surprise, he watches his unit materialize before his eyes. Heihachi's used to seeing cute girls pop up on his phone, but he's never seen one pop out of his phone! Join him on his quest to collect OP UR QTs! (That's Overpowered Ultra Rare Cuties.)

The anime stars:

• Daisuke Sakaguchi as Heihachi Okura

• Miyu Tomita as Norl Fanya (name romanization not confirmed)

• Iori Noguchi as Estel

• Ai Kayano as Shisuha Alvy

• Rie Kugimiya as Luna Varedas

The anime's staff includes:

• Chief Director: Masahiro Takada

• Director: Takashi Asami

• Series Script Supervisor: Deko Akao

• Character Designer, Chief Animation Director: Miori Suzuki

• Monster Design: Tomoyuki Abe

• Prop Design Support: Shiori Kōno

• Art Director: Kenta Tsuboi

• Background Art: Minami Takizawa (name romanization not confirmed)

• Color Key Artist: Akiko Inoue

• Compositing Director of Photography: Kōsuke Tanaka

• Offline Editing: Masaki Utsunomiya

• Offline Editing Assistant: Asuka Kojima

• Sound Director: Nobuyuki Abe

• Sound Production: On-Lead

• Music: Hiroaki Tsutsumi, George King

• Music Producer: Takahiro Ikeda

• Background Music Production Collaboration: MIRACLE BUS

• Music Production: Starry Cube

• Animation Production: Zero-G× Saber Works

• Producer: Ryō Aizawa (Starry Cube)

• Executive Producer: Kōichirō Natsume

The anime will debut in January 2027.

Chinkururi launched the story on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website in January 2016, and the series is ongoing. Micro Magazine published the ninth novel volume in August 2020.

Syū Haruno launched the manga adaptation on Comic Ride in 2018, and the 15th compiled book volume will ship on December 24.

Kaiten Books first licensed Haruno's manga adaptation in 2020. Omoi also digitally releases the manga in English. Kaiten Books released the manga's seventh volume digitally in September 2024.
author: ANN

title: Aoharu Once More Light Anime's Teaser Reveals Cast, More Staff, January 2027 Debut
content:
The official website for the light anime of Toworu Miyata 's Aoharu Once More boys' love manga unveiled a new teaser promotional video for the anime on Wednesday. The teaser announces the anime's main cast, additional staff members, and January 2027 premiere date on TV Tokyo .

The cast members include:

Tasuku Kaito as Hayato Kobayashi

Kazuki Ura a Ritsu Onishi

The newly announced staff members are Tadashi Jinbo as sound director, Toshiya Wada for sound effects, and ASLEBEN for sound production.

Tokyopop describes the manga:

Hayato Kobayashi dreams of his high school days, of the soft wind blowing by and the light streaming in through the window onto the beautiful Ritsu Onishi, and of his dazzling smile.

Rikako Machida ( Saved by the Ice Cold Prince's Embrace series composition) is directing the anime at IMAGICA Infos / Imageworks Studio . Morrigan (WAVE) is composing the music. Kazuya Takahashi is credited for production supervision.

Tokyopop licensed the manga and will release it in English.

ShuCream released the manga's first compiled book volume in June 2025.

Animate International is releasing Miyata's Living With Him , Delivery Hug Therapy , and 100dB Pouring into You manga in English. Living With Him inspired a live-action series adaptation in April 2024.

Aoharu Once More is the third project in the new boys-love label BALLOON , which launched with Dai Nippon Printing (DNP), CYBIRD , and BLUE RIGHTS last year.

The first project was the light anime adaptation of Tenma Asahi 's Saioshi no Gikei o Mederu Tame, Nagaikishimasu! (In Order to Love My Most Beloved Brother-In-Law, I'll Live a Long Life!) light novel series. The light anime premiered on January 3. OceanVeil began streaming the anime under the title I’ll Live a Long Life to Dote on My Favorite Stepbrother! on January 6.

The second project is the light anime adaptation of Kaoruko Miyama 's Perfect Addiction boys-love manga, which debuted on July 8. OceanVeil streamed the anime.

DNP spearheaded the concept of "light anime" to create animation at a lower cost on a more "timely" schedule compared to the traditional animation production workflow. The BALLOON label aims to produce four new titles in the 2026 fiscal year, with a goal of establishing a workflow capable of producing 10 or more projects a year by 2028.

title: 3 New Anime to Watch If You Miss 90s Anime
content:
1990s was the greatest decade for the anime industry, as it introduced several iconic films and series that are still loved even now. The animation styles were distinctive, and the music was unforgettable, which made them even more memorable. However, it’s not just the plot or aesthetic visuals that make these series special, as fans often have an emotional attachment to some of their childhood favorites. It was an era before streaming platforms became popular, and several Japanese anime series were made accessible worldwide on TV channels in English-dubbed formats. Anime is now a mainstream form of media, pulling in more viewers over the years. However, most beginners are often drawn to the trending modern series that take over social media discussions.

Since it can be overwhelming to find the right anime to start with, many beginners would turn to a series that recently went popular. Needless to say, while these newer series are always a good choice for anyone to start their anime journey with, there are also a bunch of older classics that are relevant to this day.

3) Lazarus

In MAPPA’s Lazarus , three years after the distribution of a miracle drug called Hapna, its creator, Dr. Skinner, reveals that it will kill everyone who took it over time. The first wave of deaths is only a month away, so it falls onto Lazarus, a covert team of former criminals assembled by the government, to track down Skinner for a cure to Hapna before humanity goes extinct. As the first new Shinichiro Watanabe project in six years and one that clearly played into Cowboy Bebop ’s iconic aesthetic, there was plenty of hype for Lazarus ’ premiere, and it initially seemed to live up to that hype. That was short-lived, however, as between the poor pacing and its lack of urgency, terrible English dub, and often nonsensical story decisions, Lazarus ultimately failed to do anything other than look good, and it’s hard to see it as anything other than Watanabe’s worst anime, by far.

2) Goodbye, Lara

The story tells a reimagined version of a fairy tale with striking visuals and a promising plot. A long time ago, a mermaid princess named Lara was raised with love by her father, the king of the sea, and her sisters. However, one day, Lara fell in love with a human prince who lived on land and yearned for him despite knowing it was a forbidden love. Falling in love with a human was not allowed in the world of mermaids, especially for a sheltered princess like her. Still, Lara journeyed to the surface world to meet him. She became human thanks to the potion given to her by the mysterious witch Grace, but it came at a steep price. Should Lara fail to find her true love, she would turn into foam and vanish into the sea. As her wish to find the man went unfulfilled, the potion took her life, and she vanished forever. However, two hundred years later, the mermaid princess is reborn in Lake Biwa and embarks on yet another journey to find her true love. Unlike last time, Lara isn’t alone and has more than enough she could ask for.

1) Dorohedoro

The story is set in an urban fantasy world where a dark and dangerous district called the Hole exists, where the strong prey on the weak. In a world where only the survival of the fittest matters, death is a daily occurrence, befitting the name of the area. The district is also a testing ground for sorcerers who take advantage of the lawless crowd and think of them as nothing more than insects. They perform experiments on those around the Hole’s hospital on a daily basis. Caiman, a half-reptile, half-man, is one such victim of such experiments, as he is cursed with his appearance and tormented by nightmares. He hunts magic users using a trusted pair of bayonets and his immunity to magic in order to find a clue to reverting to his original form. Accompanied by his female companion, Nikaido, Caiman discovers the dark secrets lingering in the alleys of the Hole while also uncovering what transpired in his past.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime in mind that you want to add here? Share your recommendations in the comments below.

title: 12 Years Ago, Naruto Reached Its Controversial Ending & It Isn’t As Bad As You Remember
content:
The legacy of the Shonen Big Three remains unmatched even though several years have passed since their debut. As the new era of the anime and manga industry began with shorter and seasonal series, fans appreciate the older generation even more with long-running stories and captivating plots. As one of the biggest Shonen classics, Naruto ‘s influence is unmatched even now. Written and illustrated by Masashi Kishimoto, Naruto became one of the most successful anime and manga franchises of all time. The story of an underdog winning the hearts of those around him and climbing to the top still inspires others.

Naruto raised an entire generation of anime fans who followed the protagonist’s journey from the beginning to the end. However, as a long-running show, it’s impossible for Naruto to be flawless. Due to years of broadcast, the anime suffered from pacing issues and inconsistent animation. Not only that, but since the manga was also serialized weekly, the anime had to release several filler episodes in between. However, apart from this, the manga also received heat for a number of reasons. It reached its controversial finale on November 10th, 2014, but luckily stood the test of time as it remains one of the most iconic Shonen Jump series in history.

Naruto Still Gets Heat For the Unresolved Plot Holes and the Final Villain

There’s no denying that the story had multiple issues throughout its run, including plot holes and the final villain. While the controversy has significantly died down over the years, certain aspects of the story are still criticized. Naruto still causes confusion with many unresolved storylines and unanswered questions. Hashirama’s fate is so famously overlooked in the story that many fans just convinced themselves that the character was so powerful, it was impossible to write how he died. Regardless, a legendary character like him deserved a better ending than fans having to guess what really happened to him. However, that’s just one example, but there are several instances where the story failed to answer major questions, including the power systems and many other plot points.

Whether it was Itachi’s illness or Orochimaru’s sudden change of heart, a lot of the things could be explored better. The final stretch of the story in particular felt rushed with so many things happening all at once. There’s really no way to sugarcoat that the final villain is still one of the most divisive moments in anime history. After hyping Madara Uchiha as the finale villain of the story, he turned out to be nothing more than a puppet of Black Zetsu. Madara’s actions were guided by Zetsu in order to free Kaguya Otsutsuki from the eternal prison her sons put her into centuries ago.

Even now, the ending often receives mixed reactions, especially in the manga that doesn’t feature an epilogue after the final war. Kaguya’s last-minute appearance shifted the flow of the story when it was just reaching its finale. With Obito joining Naruto’s side and Madara regretting his decisions, they became victims of Zetsu despite the war they started and the countless lives they took. Not to mention that Kaguya’s appearance happened with zero narrative buildup, and it seemed more like a quick way to set up the story of a sequel rather than ending the main story when it should have.

Naruto Stood the Test of Time Thanks to Its Unique and Complex Storytelling

Naruto ‘s ending is now viewed more favorably after more than a decade since the plot twist of the final villain was used as a major plot point in the sequel spin-off. The major plot twist in the final stretch of the story focused on world-building and introduced sci-fi lore to ensure the series’ longevity. Additionally, fans also pointed out how this was foreshadowed much earlier in the story, so it wasn’t something Kishimoto decided out of nowhere. Not to mention that there’s a huge change in perception when someone reads a series weekly compared to binging. Not to mention that the anime adaptation stretched out a lot of scenes and even added an epilogue, with novel adaptations that solved the problem of the rushed ending. It focused on most of the major characters and the aftermath of the war as the years went by.

Do you think Naruto’s ending deserves the criticism it received, or has it aged better now that enough time has passed? Share your thoughts in the comments below!
